hits.snippet: # Medical Robotics Startup Vexev Secures $8.6M #### Synopsis The UNSW spinout is accelerating US regulatory approval and commercial rollout of its VxWave tomographic ultrasound technology after lifting total funding to $27 million. Sydney-based medical robotics start-up Vexev has raised a $8.6m funding round, to fast-track its U.S. regulatory approval and commercialization of its VxWave ultrasound platform. Blackbird Ventures is among the investors that have backed Vexev in the past. It is a privately held firm, and therefore does not publicise revenue or profit figures. With the new funding, Vexev's total raised capital increases to $27 million and will be used for expanding its manufacturing capabilities and development of its products along with getting approval from the regulators. Vexev was established in 2018 as a spinout of the University of New South Wales (UNSW), where they're developing automated vascular imaging robotic ultrasound systems for dialysis patients. hits.title: Vexev Raises $6M to Advance VxWave Robotic Vascular Ultrasound in the U.S.
hits.snippet: Australian medical robotics company Vexev has raised $6 million to advance regulatory, manufacturing and commercialization activities for its AI-enabled robotic vascular ultrasound platform in the U.S. The latest financing brings the company’s total funding to $19 million. Vexev develops VxWave, a platform combining robotics, artificial intelligence and ultrasound imaging to automate the acquisition of diagnostic images and blood flow data from veins and arteries. The technology uses high-frequency sound waves to capture vascular ultrasound data while reducing reliance on manual image acquisition. The platform supports upper-limb imaging, with Vexev initially focusing on dialysis vascular access. Patients receiving dialysis require regular monitoring of their vascular access sites, creating a use case for more consistent and accessible imaging. hits.snippet: # Vexev Raises A$8.6 Million to Advance Australian-Built Robotic Ultrasound Platform in the United States SYDNEY, Australia, August 7, 2026 - Australian medical robotics company [Vexev](https://www.vexev.com/) today announced it has raised A$8.6 million in new funding to accelerate the path to FDA 510(k) clearance and U.S. commercialisation of VxWave, its robotic tomographic ultrasound platform. The fundraise follows successful results in a multi-site clinical study conducted with U.S. Renal Care across dialysis clinics in Texas and will support regulatory activities, manufacturing scale-up and commercial preparation. The raise brings Vexev’s total funding to A$27 million (USD$19 million). Australia has a strong history of translating local research and engineering expertise into globally adopted medical technologies. Vexev is part of the next generation leading that capability and intends to expand its manufacturing operations for the advanced robotic medical imaging platform in Surry Hills ahead of rollout to the one of the largest healthcare markets in the United States.
